Tidy a site frequency spectrum

Source: R/sfs_helpers.R
tidy.sfs.Rd

Turn an sfs object (as returned by pop_sfs(), pairwise_pop_sfs() and nwise_pop_sfs() with type = "array") into a tibble with one row per cell of the spectrum.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sfs'
tidy(x, fastest = c("last", "first"), ...)

Arguments

x

an sfs object

fastest

which population's number of allele copies changes fastest from one row to the next: "last" (the default, which keeps the order of the populations: rows are sorted by the number of copies in the first population, then in the second, and so on, as in the files written by dadi and easySFS) or "first".

...

currently unused.

Value

a tibble with one column per population (named with the population labels) giving the number of allele copies (for an unfolded spectrum, copies of the derived allele: the alternate allele, unless the loci were polarised with ancestral, in which case it is the reference allele at loci whose ancestral allele is the alternate one; for a folded spectrum, copies of the minor allele across all the populations of the spectrum), n_sites, the number of sites in that cell (a fractional number, as each locus is spread over the cells by the projection), and masked, TRUE for the cells that are masked (the corners, i.e. monomorphic sites, and for a folded spectrum the cells that were folded out). The projection of each population is stored in the attribute n_proj, and whether the spectrum is folded in the attribute folded.

Examples

example_gt <- load_example_gt("grouped_gen_tbl")

sfs <- example_gt %>% pop_sfs(n_proj = 4, type = "array")
tidy(sfs[[1]])
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>    pop1 n_sites masked
#>   <int>   <dbl> <lgl> 
#> 1     0    1.47 TRUE  
#> 2     1    2.13 FALSE 
#> 3     2    2.4  FALSE 
#> 4     3    0    TRUE  
#> 5     4    0    TRUE
